# Blueprint v0.3.4 — Deploy sets itself up + honest VRAM warnings

Three fixes from first-run testing on a 6 GB laptop.

## Deploy now provisions itself — no button-clicking

The Deploy step used to make you click through three buttons in
order: **Install runtime**, then **Pull model**, then **Start
serve**. First-time users reasonably expected the app to just get
itself ready.

It now does. On entering Deploy, Blueprint walks the sequence
automatically — installs the llama.cpp runtime, pulls the GGUF for
your selected model + quant, and starts llama-server — showing live
progress the whole way. A banner up top makes it clear the setup is
running on its own.

The manual buttons haven't gone away: if any step fails, that card
re-shows its button so you can retry by hand, and the error banner
points you to it. Each step also fires at most once per model, so
deliberately **Stop**-ing the server no longer gets undone by an
auto-restart.

## "needs more VRAM" is now a warning, not always an error

The fit badge painted every model whose *total* estimate exceeded
detected VRAM in red — even models that run fine. The total bakes in
a worst-case full-128K-context KV cache you rarely actually pay, so a
7B whose weights comfortably fit 6 GB was being flagged as if it
couldn't run at all.

Severity is now keyed off whether the **weights** fit:

- **Red (error)** — weights alone exceed VRAM: the model genuinely
  can't be GPU-resident at this quant.
- **Amber (warning)** — weights fit but the full-context total spills
  over: it runs today if you shorten context or let the KV cache
  offload to RAM. Labeled **"tight — trim context."**
- **Amber** — tight fit (70–100% of VRAM), unchanged.
- **Green** — comfortable headroom, unchanged.

## "Continue to Dashboard" now lives at the end of setup

On the Deploy step — the last step of first-time setup — the top-bar
**Back to Dashboard** button was a competing "back" affordance mid-
setup. It's now hidden on Deploy in favor of a **Continue to
Dashboard →** button that appears at the bottom once your model is
serving. The step rail's **✕ Cancel** still lets you bail out at any
point, and the top-bar button is unchanged on the Plan and Hardware
steps.

## Other platforms

All three changes are in the shared frontend, so macOS and Linux get
them too.
